stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: The construction crew assigned to the new pedestrian bridge had built dozens of steel spans over two decades, but they were ______ mass timber, the engineered wood the city had specified for this project. None of them had ever cut, joined, or load-tested the material, so the firm brought in a consultant to train them before work began.
explanation: The second sentence explains the blank: none of the crew had ever cut, joined, or load-tested mass timber, and they needed training. That describes a lack of experience, so "unfamiliar with" is the precise fit. The word "but" also sets their long steel experience against their inexperience with this material.

A.why: You picked a vivid emotion that suits a new building project. The text says nothing about how the crew felt. It only says they had no experience with the material.

B.why: You linked the crew's decades of steel work to this new material. The text says they had never worked with mass timber and needed a consultant to train them, which is the opposite of skill.

D.why: You assumed that a crew used to steel would resist a new material. The text gives no sign of objection. It describes inexperience, not opposition.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)

rated_why: Explicit contextual signal: 'never cut, joined, or load-tested'

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because they will eat almost anything, from fallen fruit to discarded food, and will den in drainage culverts or beneath porches, coyotes are remarkably ______ city life. Wildlife surveys now record stable coyote populations in the parks and residential neighborhoods of many large North American cities.
explanation: The word "Because" ties the blank to the coyotes' flexible diet and denning habits. The next sentence adds that they live in stable numbers in cities. An animal that can use whatever food and shelter a city offers is "adaptable to" city life.

A.why: You went with a common idea about wild animals and cities. The text shows coyotes thriving in parks and neighborhoods, which does not fit an animal that fears city life.

C.why: You chose a strong negative phrase. Nothing in the text suggests that coyotes resist or damage city life. They make use of it.

D.why: You chose a phrase about a lack of awareness. The coyotes are actively using city food and shelter, so they are hardly ignorant of city life.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)

rated_why: Clear evidence of adaptability from eating habits and denning behavior

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Officials planning a mobile blood-pressure clinic in the county expected residents to be wary of it, since earlier outreach programs had drawn few visitors. Instead, residents proved ______ the clinic: within its first month, more than 900 people stopped by for a screening, and many returned for follow-up visits.
explanation: The word "Instead" reverses the officials' expectation that residents would be wary. The colon then introduces the evidence: 900 visitors in a month, many of whom came back. Residents were willing to accept and use the clinic, so "receptive to" fits.

B.why: You chose a strong negative reaction, perhaps because the topic is health. "Instead" signals the opposite of wariness, and hundreds of people chose to visit.

C.why: You overlooked the numbers. More than 900 visits and many return visits show the opposite of indifference.

D.why: You invented a problem the text never mentions. Nothing suggests that residents misunderstood the clinic, and their heavy use of it points the other way.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)

rated_why: Strong contrast signal with quantified support (900+ visitors)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Popular histories often portray the handloom weavers of northern England as enraged by the arrival of the power loom. Parish records from one weaving village suggest a different picture: many weavers there were simply ______ the new machines. They neither smashed the looms nor sought work in the mills; they went on weaving by hand as before, apparently without complaint.
explanation: The phrase "a different picture" rejects the image of enraged weavers. The last sentence defines the blank: the weavers neither attacked the machines nor adopted them, and they carried on without complaint. That neutral lack of concern is "indifferent to."

A.why: You assumed that machines always take over workers' lives. These weavers kept weaving by hand and did not seek mill work, so they did not depend on the new looms.

B.why: You swung from anger to its opposite. The text describes weavers who simply carried on, not weavers who welcomed the looms. Enthusiasm goes further than the evidence.

C.why: You chose the vivid phrase that matches the popular story. The text calls its evidence "a different picture," so the blank has to depart from anger, not repeat it.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Supporting details explicitly rule out other options ('neither smashed nor sought work')

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When the painter Mira Olsen arrived at the print studio in 1998, she was ______ etching. She had never coated a copper plate with wax, scratched a design through it, or lowered a plate into an acid bath, and she spent her first weeks watching the studio's master printer at work.
explanation: The second sentence defines the blank. Olsen had never done any of the basic steps of etching, and she began by watching someone else. She was inexperienced, so "new to" is the precise fit.

A.why: You chose a vivid emotion that suits a hard, unfamiliar craft. The text describes only her lack of experience. It never says she struggled or felt annoyed.

C.why: You assumed that an artist at a print studio must be committed to printmaking. The text stresses that she had never tried etching, which gives no basis for devotion.

D.why: You matched the phrase to her identity as an artist. She could not be famous for a technique she had never practiced.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Folklorist Ines Varga did not go looking for unusual versions of the tales she studied, but she was ______ them when they turned up. Rather than dismissing a telling that departed from the familiar plot, she recorded it in full and filed it alongside the more common versions, treating it as equally worth preserving.
explanation: The word "but" contrasts not seeking out variants with how Varga responded to them. The next sentence shows her accepting and recording each one. Willingness without active pursuit is being "open to" them.

A.why: You chose the intense phrase because she recorded every variant. The text says she did not go looking for them, which rules out obsession. The logic calls for a milder attitude.

B.why: You missed "when they turned up." She noticed these versions and recorded them in full, so she could not have been unaware of them.

D.why: You read "did not go looking for" as a lack of interest. She treated each variant as equally worth preserving, which is not boredom.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Action details establish receptiveness ('recorded in full, treated as equally worth preserving')

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Paleobotanist Dana Kwame spent a decade sorting fossil pollen grains under the microscope, sometimes examining several thousand in a single week. She therefore became highly ______ telling apart grains from closely related plant species, a task that often defeats newcomers to the field because the differences can be a fraction of a micrometer.
explanation: The word "therefore" means the blank must follow from ten years of sorting thousands of grains. That much repetition builds skill, and the contrast with struggling newcomers confirms it. "Practiced at" is the logical result.

B.why: You picked up on how hard the task is for newcomers. The passage contrasts Kwame with those newcomers, and a decade of practice leads to skill, not anxiety.

C.why: You chose a phrase about a reaction to something new. After ten years of the same work, surprise does not follow from "therefore."

D.why: You chose a negative attitude the text never suggests. She spent a decade doing this work, and nothing indicates that she objects to it.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Simple cause-effect: years of practice produces skill

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: The town of Valle Seco sits near several active faults and experiences dozens of minor tremors each year, most too weak to damage buildings. Long-time residents have therefore become ______ the shaking: when a small quake rattles the windows, most barely look up from their work.
explanation: The word "therefore" ties the blank to years of frequent, harmless tremors. The colon then shows the result: residents barely react. Repeated exposure that makes something ordinary means they are "accustomed to" it.

A.why: You chose a phrase about interest. Residents who barely look up are not curious. The text describes routine acceptance.

B.why: You matched the phrase to the town's location rather than to the residents' attitude. People cannot cause earthquakes, and the blank describes how they react to the shaking.

C.why: You chose the vivid reaction that earthquakes usually call to mind. The text says the tremors are minor and residents barely react, so the logic calls for a calm response, not terror.

subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Behavioral evidence ('barely look up') directly confirms habituation
